approach: In both setups every pulley is fixed to the overhead bracket, so each pulley only changes the direction of the pull, never the size of the force needed.

steps.text: In figure (i), a single fixed pulley redirects the string from the block to the person's hand; the tension in the string equals the block's weight.
In figure (ii), both pulleys are also fixed to the bracket and neither is attached to the block, so one string still carries a single tension from the block to the person's hand.
A fixed pulley only changes the direction of a force, never its size, so the person pulls with the same force in both cases.
steps.why_this_step: Only a pulley attached to the moving load, not fixed to a support, can reduce the force needed.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the two pulleys in figure (ii) form a movable-pulley system that halves the force needed, when neither pulley is attached to the block.
